newsitem.title: USA: US stocks up at midday, near record high.
newsitem.headline: US stocks up at midday, near record high.

text.p: U.S. stocks were higher at midday, with the Dow just a whisker away from its all-time high, after the U.S.Producer Price Index showed tame inflation.

Bonds rose after the August PPI was released early this morning. Weekly jobless claims came in higher than expected, further calming fears about the extent of a possible interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 31 points to 5786, just shy of its record high of 5796.10, reached on May 23. The Nasdaq Composite climbed seven points to 1161.
"The PPI made the market happy, and tomorrow's CPI (Consumer Price Index) is seen relatively stable," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
"The economic picture is becoming clearer, so here we are with the Dow right at its all-time high," he said.
PPI rose 0.3 percent, while the "core rate" fell 0.1 percent. Analysts had expected rises of 0.1 percent for both measures.
"We didn't really have a summer rally and we're coming into a season that is historically weak. The market may surprise us and buck the trend," Bleier said.
Edgar Peters, chief investment strategist at PanAgora Asset Management Inc, said fresh highs for the market could be cause for concern.

"Our models are getting more and more bearish. We're neutral on bonds, modestly bearish on equities...," he said. "In the short-term, stocks look risky. The upside going on is purely speculative, for no fundamental reason."

He added, "I think people are counting on the Fed stimulating another slowdown, but we have full employment and wage inflation...The only way to get rid of wage inflation is to throw people out of work -- meaning recession."
